title: Kanak Bhawan Ayodhya - The Golden Palace of Divine Love
content:
Kanak Bhawan Ayodhya

Kanak Bhawan, located in the heart of Ayodhya near Hanuman Garhi, is one of the most beloved temples dedicated to Lord Rama and Goddess Sita. Known as the “Palace of Gold,” this sacred shrine stands as a shining symbol of devotion, purity, and the eternal love of Ram-Sita. With its golden idols, peaceful ambience, and rich history, Kanak Bhawan is a must-visit for every pilgrim in Ayodhya.

History & Significance

According to legend, Kanak Bhawan was originally gifted to Goddess Sita by Queen Kaikeyi as a wedding present after her marriage to Shri Ram. The term “Kanak” means gold, reflecting the belief that Kaikeyi adorned Sita with a golden palace filled with love, joy, and blessings.

The current temple structure was constructed in 1891 by the Queen of Tikamgarh, Vrishbhanu Kunwari, and is a stunning example of Rajput and Awadhi architectural blend.

Today, the temple remains a place where devotees feel the warmth and serenity of Ram-Sita’s divine presence.

Architecture & Spiritual Charm

Kanak Bhawan is beautifully built with:

  • White stone walls glowing under the sun
  • Elegant domes and arches
  • Colorful murals depicting Ramayana stories
  • Peaceful courtyards for meditation

The highlight is the three golden idols of Lord Ram and Goddess Sita, adorned with intricate jewelry. When the aarti takes place, the idols shine radiantly, filling the entire space with divine energy.

Why Visit Kanak Bhawan?

1. Peaceful & Divine Atmosphere: A calming place where you can sit, pray, or meditate without disturbance.

2. Beautiful Golden Idols: The sight of Ram-Sita in golden attire is incredibly heartwarming and spiritually uplifting.

3. Rich Historical Connection: Linked to Sita Mata’s marriage and her life in Ayodhya.

4. Close to Major Attractions: Located near Hanuman Garhi and Ram Janmabhoomi, making it easy to cover in a short walk.

Location

  • City: Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh
  • Nearby Landmark: 300 meters from Hanuman Garhi
  • Easily accessible from all parts of Ayodhya town.

Temple Timings

  • Morning: 6:00 AM - 11:00 AM
  • Evening: 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM
    Aarti times may vary during festivals.

Best Time to Visit

  • October to March for pleasant weather
  • During festivals like Ram Navami, Diwali, and Vivah Panchami for grand celebrations

Nearby Attractions

  • Ram Mandir (Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple)
  • Hanuman Garhi
  • Sita Rasoi
  • Dashrath Mahal
  • Nageshwarnath Temple
  • Treta Ke Thakur

Travel Tips

  • Wear comfortable clothes suitable for temples
  • Photography may be restricted inside - follow rules
  • Visit early morning to avoid crowds
  • Remove footwear at the entrance area
  • Keep valuables secure
excerpt: Kanak Bhawan in Ayodhya is a serene temple dedicated to Ram and Sita, known for its golden idols and peaceful atmosphere. Gifted to Sita by Kaikeyi, it represents divine love and royal blessings. A must-visit spiritual spot for every Ayodhya traveler.
